etch.model: front reflection = Fresnel x (specular_fraction x mirror image of the room light + the rest blurred by a Gaussian lobe of lobe_sigma_deg)
etch.derived: gloss 69 = 69 % of polished glass's flux inside the 60 degree gloss aperture (4.4 x 11.7 degrees); the lobe holds that flux less the specular part
assumed: the gloss is the standard 60 degree geometry (ASTM D523)
the lobe is Gaussian and the same at every angle
the 5151's etch is like Philips' etched display glass
etch.ref: Nuijs & Horikx, Diffraction and scattering at antiglare structures for display devices, Applied Optics 33 (1994) 4058, Table 1 (Philips Research; etched glass)

faceplate.ref: Philips T16 1987: light transmission about 50 % (normal tint), etched anti-glare option

name: Commodore 1084S colour monitor, P22 slot-mask tube (PAL RGB)

timing.ref: PAL: 64 us lines, 52 us active, 312 lines per 50 Hz field; Amiga 640 x 256 (Commodore 1084S manual)

drive.mapping: each gun's beam current = (signal)^2.4, signal = the art's sRGB channel (analogue RGB 0.7 V p-p)
drive.ref: ITU-R BT.1886 (CRT reference: gamma 2.4); Commodore 1084S manual (analogue RGB input)

phosphor.type: P22 (EBU set): Y2O2S:Eu red, ZnS:Cu,Al green, ZnS:Ag blue
facts: P22: red Y2O2S:Eu, green ZnS:Cu,Al, blue ZnS:Ag
EBU Tech 3213: red 0.64, 0.33; green 0.29, 0.60; blue 0.15, 0.06; balanced to D65 white
Kuhn 2002, photomultiplier fits of a P22 monitor: red gone within 1-2 ms; green and blue have a slow power-law tail
the frame after a hit still shows 5.2 % (green) and 4.6 % (blue) of its light: faint trails in a dark room; red none
refs: Kuhn, Optical Time-Domain Eavesdropping Risks of CRT Displays, IEEE Symposium on Security and Privacy 2002
EBU Tech 3213, Chromaticity tolerances for studio monitors

colour.note: Three layers in linear light, balanced so equal drive gives D65 white.

spot.note: no spot size is published for the M34EAQ; sigma 0.25 mm at full drive (assumed)

bloom.model: sigma(drive) = sigma_mm * (drive / efficiency_vs_P4) ** power; drive = beam signal relative to full drive, held at min_drive_fraction or above (the measured currents span a factor of 4)
bloom.ref: Philips T16 1987, Resolution characteristics, Fig. 5 (M31-336..350, 12 kV): line width at 50, 75, 100, 200 uA, traced into tools/philips-m31-line-width.json

raster.note: 288 lines fill the 198 mm picture height of a 13 in viewable 4:3 tube; the panel shows the 256-line picture

mask.note: vertical R G B phosphor stripes of equal width; the slots' bridges are not modelled
mask.ref: Commodore 1084S manual; Philips CM8833-II service manual (M34EAQ, slot triplet pitch 0.42 mm)

contrast.note: video gain (IBM: 'increases the brightness of the data')

brightness.note: uniform beam on every line (IBM: 'increases the brightness of the entire screen'); fraction of full drive

facts: Commodore 1084S: 14 in (13 in viewable), 90°, Philips M34EAQ slot-mask tube, 25 kV
15.625 kHz lines, 50 Hz frames, 256-line picture (Amiga) within 288 visible lines
analogue RGB 0.7 V p-p; each gun's beam follows the signal to the power 2.4 (BT.1886)
slot mask, 0.42 mm triplet pitch: vertical red, green and blue stripes, drawn where this display gives each stripe 2 or more pixels
the 5151 profile's glass, etch and room; full drive 100 cd/m2
